chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever backbites a believing warrior, harms him, or speaks ill of his family, a stand will be made for him on the Day of Resurrection, and his good deeds will be exhausted, then he will be thrust headlong into the Fire if the warrior was obedient to Allah, Exalted and Glorious.'
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for backbiting a believing warrior in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the elevated status of the *ghazi* (warrior in God's cause) by specifying that backbiting or harming them consumes the offender's good deeds entirely, leading to a headlong plunge into Hellfire. This narration underscores the practical implication that spiritual merit is fragile when one attacks the dignity of those actively engaged in divine obedience, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the rights of the believer.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) narrates from his ancestors that the  Holy  Prophet  (s.a.w.s.)  said,  “One  who  backbites  a believing warrior or hurts him or his family members, this deed will be stored at a place which will destroy all of his good deeds and he will be thrown headlong into Hell if the warrior was obedient to Allah.”
